brief: inline dispatch: Argonian tribes — CF-C023 gap (Agacephs/Paatru/Archein/Sarpa/Dead-Water/Miredancers all zero occurrences)
outputs_written: corpus/60-lore/RI-LOR08-argonian-tribes.md — the design note, written BEFORE any content. Six peoples, all canon-named, zero invented; a rejected-names table so every omission is a decision; the five-axis differentiation test; the Xul-Aneekh reframed as a consensus OF peoples; 6 registered disputes and 5 deliberately unregistered arguments; measured tooling section; comparison method, scoring, how-we-lose, provenance.
game/data/npcs/tribes.json — 11 NPCs across 5 settlements, new faction ids agacephs/paatru/sarpa/archein/miredancers/dead-water.
game/data/dialogue/topics/75-tribes.json — 12 topics, 62 infos, 2771 w. 7 dispute topics (cf+pos), 5 argument topics with no cf at all.

game/data/books/the-peoples.json — 4 books, 2310 w: A Survey of the Peoples of the Interior (T1, Imperial), The Grange Book (T6, Archein), The Descents (T4, Miredancer rootpost record), Told at the Weir (T4, a lukiul factor's failed errand).
game/data/dialogue/rumours.json — 7 tribal rumours added across helstrom/gideon/lilmoth/thorn/blackrose/soulrest, all adds_topics resolving.
corpus/60-lore/data/canon-facts.json — CF-D022..CF-D027 (6 disputes, 66 positions total in registry) + CF-C025..CF-C030 (one constructed fact per people). Registry 71 -> 83 facts, 21 -> 27 disputed.

tools/lore/tribe-census.mjs — NEW, the tool RI-LOR08's comparison method names. Refuses to count mentions: presence (body/mouth/text), registered position, refusal, and the pairwise axis-collision arithmetic. --self-test 9/9, each check broken on purpose.
findings: W1-23 report §6 is the binding context: province is organised by 4 CONSTRUCTED bodies (Deep-Kin 87, Xul-Aneekh 84, Drowned Court 64, Sap-Cutters 53, Wet Ledger 45), not tribes. Its explicit warning: 'If tribes are wanted, they need a faction each, not a mention each.'
Ruling from lore builder (W1-23 §4): a contradiction is a disagreement about what IS THE CASE; a disagreement about what is WORTH DOING is an argument. Register the first, write the second.

Registry now has real consumers: tools/lore/build-canon.mjs projects corpus/60-lore/data/canon-facts.json -> game/data/lore/canon.json with authorially_true replaced by truth_seal. converse.js infoFor() gates infos by cf+pos against holders.
21 disputes registered, 71 facts, as of W1-23. canon-census.mjs is the gate tool (not wired into CI on purpose).
Faction ids are spelled two ways on NPC records (drowned-court vs the_drowned_court etc) - any new tribe id must pick ONE and check world/canon.js#fold().

SOURCE MINE (uesp extract): Agacephs/Paatru/Sarpa named in Lore:The Argonian Account Book 4 — Agacephs are interior, near the Hist, 'finding little in the outside world worth seeing'; Nagas, toad-like Paatru and winged Sarpa 'would have killed him on the spot'.

SOURCE: Archeins are canon and are the answer to the lease finding — PGE 3rd ed: Imperials rule the coast but 'most have native Argonians as advisors. These Archeins also act as governors in the rural areas'. The Argonian Account Bk4 calls them 'pompous, assimilated, slaver kleptocrats'; ESO's From Argonian to Saxhleel calls them 'Archein tribe scum in the employ of House Dres'. Plantation east of Gideon (Archein Right-Foot-Rock) sells a she-worker's twins to 'a good trader in town'.

SOURCE: Tribes of Murkmire (7 books, Emmanubeth Hurrent) gives the canonical DIFFERENTIATION MODEL: Jel name + Tamrielic name; one distinguishing craft; one distinguishing taboo; Miredancers = Gee-Rusleel (piety, Sap-Speaker, sap-poisoning: gold tongue, bark scale); Dead-Water = Naga-Kur (wear pieces of fallen comrades so they 'fight after death too'); Root-House = Tum-Taleel; Black-Tongues = Kota-Vimleel (alchemy, Shadowscale breeding, Gloom Nectar); Ghost People = Veeskhleel (dead-stealers); Bright-Throats = Wasseek-haleel (seed dolls).

SOURCE: 'Tribal Connections' is the load-bearing one — tribes raid each other and forgive, because reincarnation makes tribe membership fluid ('A Black-Tongue may become a Miredancer in the fullness of time'), and because they are INTERDEPENDENT by design. And 'As many as the lights' = the count of tribes is deliberately uncountable.

MECHANICS: game/src/world/canon.js — holders match on actor OR faction, narrowed by races/settlements; a speaker matching TWO positions gets NEITHER. fold() normalises id spellings. resolve() THROWS at boot on: a topics[] entry that is not a dialogue topic in the build, a voiced_by book/npc/dialogue#actor that does not exist, or a position with no holders. So content must land BEFORE registration.

GEOGRAPHY: region->settlement map is blackwood>Gideon, crimson-coast>Archon, stone-forest>Helstrom, stone-wastes>Soulrest, thornmarsh>Thorn, western-rootlands>Lilmoth+Blackrose, salt-hills>Stormhold. clay-moor, deep-marshes, eastern-rootlands, hive, marauders-coast, valus-ridge have NO settlement — those are the tribes' ground.

PROSE BARS (tools/check-prose.mjs): questions floor 39.8/10k (ref 159.2), exclamations band floor 5.3 (ref 21.3), sting ceiling 6.0 (ref 3.4), andopen band floor 16.0 (ref 64.0), contractions band 43.8-365.4 (ref 292.3). Tics: 'that is what/why/all', -body forms, 'eleven', sentence-initial 'Which' fragments.

MEASURED at b51789e. Registry 21 -> 27 disputes, 27/27 fully voiced. Contradiction edges 50 -> 57, unregistered 0. Topics on which two REAL shipped people give incompatible registered answers: 4 -> 10. Perturbation (lines that vanish when a holder is struck): 11/11 -> 43/43. Reach 336/336 -> 347/347. Dated/undated-horizon facts 12 (8 pre-3E) -> 14 (10 pre-3E).

The fail-closed assertion was tested, not assumed: pointing CF-D027/A at an actor no NPC carries takes boot-check from PASS to a thrown 'canon register: 1 unresolved reference'. Content landed before registration, per the brief.

PROSE: all four authored files pass every gated bar. 75-tribes.json questions 50.5 (floor 39.8), exclamations 14.4 (band 5.3-42.6), sting 0.00 (ceiling 6.0), fragopen 0.00, andopen 36.1, contractions 115.5, zero tics. the-peoples.json (books register) questions 17.2 (floor 8.2), exclamations 8.6, sting 0.00, andopen 21.5, contractions 30.0, zero tics. rumours.json went from 6 failing bars to clean (others had already fixed most of it; my 3 -body forms were the last).

The de-contraction of the interior peoples' voices was a register decision that the metric happened to want too: Agaceph/Paatru/Sarpa/Dead-Water/Sap-Speaker speak Tamrielic formally, Archein and Imperials contract. Contraction rate fell 416.8 -> 115.5 per 10k and the file reads as two registers rather than one.

DELIBERATELY NOT REGISTERED, under W1-23's ruling: whether the coast should be emptied; whether an outsider may be guided inland; whether the Sap-Speaker should keep drinking; whether a lukiul may be buried at a well; whether the Archein factor/quay distinction is a distinction. All five are written as arguments with heat and carry no cf. The last one is the sharpest case — registering it would flatter it.
next_step: none for the builder. Open for a critic: (1) the axis table in tribe-census.mjs is TRANSCRIBED from RI-LOR08 §2, not derived — a builder who changed §2 and not the table would pass; (2) Paatru/Sarpa/Archein each appear in only one shipped book; (3) Ghost People and Root-House People are left on the table on purpose as the wave-2 additions.
notes_for_successor: Complete. Browser used once, for boot-check + the deliberate fail-closed perturbation, at loadavg 17 with 24 browsers — a boolean, not a timing, so contention does not touch it. Did not commit.

reverified.note: files_touching in this record names game/data/books/the-tribes.json but the shipped, indexed file is game/data/books/the-peoples.json (outputs_written above has it right) -- a stale filename in one field, not a missing deliverable. game/data/index.json confirms npcs/tribes.json (id: tribes) and books/the-peoples.json are both indexed, so the running game loads them; the brief's premise that tribes.json was 'not yet in index.json' predates this piece landing.
